title: 第十九章 玄渊阁第二十章 蒙训院
slug: 纳玄尘第五十三章安凌
content_zh:
;;
密室里很安静。
只有墙上那盏油灯的火苗在轻轻晃动，把影子拉长又缩短，一遍一遍。
苏尘坐在密室正中的蒲团上，手掌摊开，一枚中品玄铢搁在掌心。玄铢表面的乌亮光泽已经暗淡了大半——里面的能量被他抽得七七八八了。
他闭上眼睛，将最后一丝能量沿经脉引了一遍。
能量走过手臂，过肩，入胸口，沿着那条他已经走了三年的路线，在经脉中缓缓推进。三年前这条经脉细得像一根棉线，能量走不到三寸就散了。现在他能清晰地感知到整条经脉的走向——像一条干涸了多年的河道，终于重新有了水流。
那股能量一路向下，汇入丹田。
丹田里，一层隐约的屏障就在那里。薄薄的，像一层膜，但就是过不去。
苏尘没有强行冲击。他让那股能量在丹田外停了停，然后慢慢地、稳稳地推了过去。
屏障破了。
像一层薄冰被温水化开，没有声响，没有剧痛。只有一股温热的感觉从丹田漫开，沿着经脉缓缓流向四肢百骸。
苏尘睁开眼，低头看了看自己的手。
掌心那枚中品玄铢已经彻底暗淡了——灰扑扑的，像一块普通的石头。
他把玄铢搁在膝上，呼出一口气。
开脉境入境。
五年。从一个连纳气法都运转不动的病秧子，到开脉境，花了整整五年。比正常修炼者慢得多——人家有天赋的，两年就能走完这条路。但他起步时才十岁，经脉又细又弱，拿的还是一本最烂的市面货色。
五年就五年吧。
苏尘把废掉的玄铢收进旁边的木匣里，站起身，活动了一下肩膀。骨头咔咔响了几声。他坐了一整天了，腿有点麻。
他看了一眼墙角——那里堆着三只木箱，里面装的全是消耗掉的中品玄铢。前两年用下品，速度太慢了，他后来咬咬牙全部换成了中品。一枚中品等于一百枚下品，吸收效率还要高出不少——虽然贵，但省时间。钱嘛，瀚北王府的世子还不至于花不起这点修炼钱。
他推开密室的门，沿着地道的台阶往上走。

地道比三年前宽敞多了。以前就是一条仅容一人通过的窄缝，弯着腰才能走。现在扩到了将近一人宽，顶部也加高了，成年人走起来不用低头。两侧的土墙每隔几步就嵌了一盏油灯，灯芯是新换的，火苗烧得正旺。
三年前这地下只有三间小室——一间练功的、一间存东西的、一间放材料的。
现在已经不是了。
三天前，最后一面墙砌好，最后一条通风道打通。老周带着那班从外地找来的工匠，在地下忙了五年，终于把这片地下空间扩成了他想要的样子。
苏尘沿着通道走了一段。
左手边第一间是藏书室——不是书房，是藏书室。三年前那间堆满杂书和药方的小室已经被推掉了，取而代之的是一间两丈见方的石室。靠墙打了整排的架子，上头摆着老周这些年从各地搜罗来的东西——几本修炼杂记、一册朔州军方流传出来的军阵图解、半本从黑市上淘来的丹药笔记、还有那本无名中品功法残本，被单独放在一只铁匣里，锁着。
右手边是档案室。搁物架刚搬进去，还空荡荡的——里面目前只放了苏尘手写的几页纸，记录了他对无名中品功法的研究心得，以及一些暗桩联络的要点备忘。以他前世打理玄镜司的习惯，这间屋子迟早会填满。
藏书室和档案室之间的通道继续往前，围出一块不小的空间。摆了一张长桌和几把矮凳——能容十来人围坐议事，平时空着，偶尔老周从庄子上带信回来，就在这里坐下来谈。
再往前走，大厅另一侧，通道出口正对面是一间密室。
比原来的练功静室大了将近五倍。顶上嵌了几块打磨过的晶石，能把地面上的光折射下来，白天的时候不需要点灯也看得见。地面铺了青砖，正中央摆了一只蒲团——就是他刚才坐了整整一天的地方。墙角的架子上整齐地码着十来枚中品玄铢和半盒碎晶。旁边的小几上搁着一壶冷茶和一只空碗。
苏尘在三年前那间小密室里练功，总觉得憋屈。转身都嫌挤。现在这间，他在里面打一套拳都绰绰有余了。
密室里还有一条支道，通向一间更小的石室——应急藏身处。里面备了水、干粮、一套换洗衣裳、几枚零散的下品玄铢。万一出了什么事，人可以在这里躲上七八天。粮食和饮水定时更新，老周安排的。
苏尘推开正屋床板，从密道口爬了上去。
正屋里的摆设和平时一样——床铺铺得整整齐齐，桌上搁着一只粗瓷茶壶和一只倒扣的碗。阳光从窗户透进来，在地板上画出一块方方正正的光斑。
他走到门口，推开门。
秋天的风迎面扑来，带着干草、马粪和泥土混合的气味。太阳已经偏西了，但光线还很足。院子里的老槐树的叶子黄了大半，风一吹，稀稀拉拉地往下掉。
刘叔在马厩那边，正蹲在地上修理一副旧马鞍。他看见苏尘从正屋里出来，放下手里的活计站了起来：
“少主。好了？“

It was quiet in the secret room.
Only the flame of the oil lamp on the wall swayed gently, lengthening and shortening the shadow over and over again.
Su Chen sat on the futon in the middle of the secret room, with his palms spread out and a middle-grade Xuan Baht resting on his palm. The shiny black luster on the surface of Xuan Zhu has been mostly dimmed - the energy inside has been drained away by him.
He closed his eyes and channeled the last bit of energy along his meridians.
The energy traveled through his arms, over his shoulders, and into his chest, slowly advancing through his meridians along the route he had taken for three years. Three years ago, this meridian was as thin as a cotton thread, and the energy dissipated within three inches. Now he can clearly feel the direction of the entire meridian - like a river that has been dry for many years and finally has water flowing again.
The energy went all the way down and merged into the Dantian.
In the dantian, a vague barrier is there. It's thin, like a membrane, but it just can't get through.
Su Chen did not attack forcefully. He let the energy pause outside his Dantian, and then slowly and steadily pushed it forward.
The barrier is broken.
Like a thin layer of ice being melted away by warm water, there was no sound or severe pain. There is only a warm feeling that spreads from the Dantian and slowly flows along the meridians to the limbs and bones.
Su Chen opened his eyes and looked down at his hands.
The middle-grade Xuan Baht in the palm of my hand has completely dimmed - gray, like an ordinary stone.
He put Xuan Bah on his knees and exhaled.
Entering the Kaimai Realm.
Five years. It took five years to go from a sick young man who couldn't even operate the Naqi method to the state of opening the pulse. Much slower than normal practitioners - those with talent can complete this path in two years. But he was only ten years old when he started, his meridians were thin and weak, and he had the worst book on the market.
Just five years.
Su Chen put the discarded Xuan Bah into the wooden box next to him, stood up, and moved his shoulders. The bones cracked several times. He had been sitting all day and his legs were a little numb.
He glanced at the corner - there were three wooden boxes piled there, filled with consumed middle-grade Xuan Baht. In the first two years, he used low-grade products, which were too slow. Later, he gritted his teeth and replaced them all with medium-grade products. One medium-grade product is equal to a hundred low-grade products, and the absorption efficiency is much higher - although it is expensive, it saves time. As for money, the prince of Hanbei Palace can't afford this little money for cultivation.
He pushed open the door to the secret room and walked up the tunnel steps.
The tunnels are much wider than they were three years ago. It used to be a narrow gap that only allowed one person to pass through, and he had to bend down to walk through it. Now it has been expanded to nearly a person's width, and the top has been raised, so adults don't have to lower their heads when walking. An oil lamp was embedded in the earthen walls on both sides every few steps. The wick was newly replaced and the flame was burning brightly.
Three years ago, there were only three small rooms in this underground room - one for practicing, one for storing things, and one for storing materials.
Not anymore.
Three days ago, the last wall was built and the last ventilation channel was opened. Lao Zhou and his group of craftsmen brought in from other places worked underground for five years, and finally expanded the underground space into what he wanted.
Su Chen walked along the passage for a while.
The first room on the left is the library—not a study, but a library. The small room filled with miscellaneous books and prescriptions three years ago has been demolished and replaced by a two-foot-square stone room. A whole row of shelves were built against the wall, and on them were things that Lao Zhou had collected from various places over the years - several training journals, a volume of military formation diagrams circulated by the Shuozhou military, half a book of elixir notes bought from the black market, and the remains of an unknown middle-grade exercise technique, which were placed alone in an iron box and locked.
On the right is the archives room. The shelf had just been moved in, and it was still empty - there were only a few pages of Su Chen's handwriting in it, recording his research experience on the unknown middle-grade exercises, as well as some memos on key points for secret contact. Based on his habit of managing the Xuanjing Division in his previous life, this room would be filled sooner or later.The passage between the library and the archives continues forward, enclosing a large space. A long table and several low stools were set up, which could accommodate about ten people to sit around and discuss matters. It was usually empty. Occasionally, when Lao Zhou came back from Zhuangzi with a letter, he would sit here and talk.
Going further, on the other side of the hall, directly opposite the passage exit, is a secret room.
It is nearly five times larger than the original practice quiet room. There are a few polished crystals embedded on the top, which can refract the light from the ground. It can be seen during the day without lighting a lamp. The floor was paved with blue bricks, and a futon was placed in the center - the same place where he had been sitting all day. On the shelf in the corner were neatly stacked a dozen mid-grade Xuan Baht and half a box of broken crystals. There is a pot of cold tea and an empty bowl on the small table next to it.
Su Chen always felt aggrieved while practicing in the small secret room three years ago. It's too crowded even when you turn around. Now in this room, he can do a set of punches more than enough.
There is also a branch passage in the secret room that leads to a smaller stone room-an emergency hiding place. It contained water, dry food, a change of clothes, and a few scattered low-grade xuan baht. If something happens, people can hide here for seven or eight days. Food and drinking water are regularly updated, arranged by Lao Zhou.
Su Chen pushed aside the bed board in the main room and climbed up from the secret passage.
The furnishings in the main room were the same as usual - the bed was neatly made, and there was a rough porcelain teapot and an upside-down bowl on the table. The sunlight filtered in through the window, drawing a square spot of light on the floor.
He walked to the door and opened it.
The autumn wind blew against my face, carrying the smell of hay, horse manure and earth. The sun was already in the west, but there was still plenty of light. Most of the leaves of the old locust tree in the yard have turned yellow, and they fall sparsely when the wind blows.
Uncle Liu was over there in the stable, squatting on the ground repairing an old saddle. He saw Su Chen come out of the main room, put down his work and stood up:
"Young Master. Are you ready?"
